Customer to provision VPC peering details and IP allowlist by 2026-11-16
CSM to share onboarding runbook and sprint 0 checklist
action_items: Dev Patel: Run smoke benchmark with c5n-equivalent instance and share tail latency PDF (due 2026-11-18)
Lena Ortiz: Confirm data residency requirement and whether PII tuning is needed (due 2026-11-16)
Aisha Khan: Send list of required compliance certifications and internal auditors contact (due 2026-11-15)

header: Date: 2026-11-11 | Start: 16:00 PST | Duration: 58 min | Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Dev Patel (Redwood SE), Anika Suresh (CSM); Lena Ortiz, Samuel Pike, Aisha Khan, Tom Reynolds, Priya Nair (Cypress Grid)
summary: Orientation call to align on activation sprint 0, security gating items, pilot scope, and next steps. Main points: customer prefers private VPC deployment with SOC2 requirements, wants predictable latency for inference at 99th percentile, interested in a 4-week pilot on Dedicated capacity with a follow-up production migration plan. Action items and a benchmark run were agreed.
topics: VPC / private deployment options and IP peering
Pilot scope: throughput/latency targets and dataset constraints
Pricing and Dedicated capacity vs Hosted tradeoffs
Integration points: RBAC, audit logs, and runbooks
transcript:
[16:00] Maria Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maria from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Quick roll call?
[16:03] Lena Ortiz: Lena here, Head of Platform at Cypress Grid.
[16:04] Samuel Pike: Sam, SRE.
[16:05] Aisha Khan: Aisha, security.
[16:06] Tom Reynolds: Tom, director of ML.
[16:06] Priya Nair: Priya product.
[16:07] Dev Patel: Dev from Redwood SE, I'll own the bench and infra topics today.
[16:08] Maria Chen: Cool, objective for today is to align on the activation sprint 0 and the pilot scope, clarify security blockers and handoffs. We'll take notes and leave with concrete next steps.
[16:12] Tom Reynolds: High level — we run inference as part of our realtime routing stack. Need 50 qps steady with occasional bursts to 200 for peak. 99th percentile latency target is sub-200ms for 512-token-ish requests.
[16:13] Dev Patel: Got it, that's helpful. When you say 512, is that typical or worst-case?
[16:13] Tom Reynolds: Typical, but sometimes we go to 1,024 for long form.
[16:14] Maria Chen: Noted. On Redwood side we can propose a pilot on Dedicated capacity to get predictable tails, or we can start hosted to iterate faster. Any preference?
[16:15] Lena Ortiz: We're leaning private — VPC peering and strict egress controls. Compliance team said no public-cloud-hosted APIs for now.
[16:16] Aisha Khan: Yeah, must be in our VPC. Also need KMS integration and key rotation policy. SOC2 is a minimum and we might require additional controls.
[16:18] Dev Patel: Private deployment path is fine — we have a private control plane option and an on-prem package. For KMS we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. Small note: some kernel-level optimizations depend on GPU types for quantized models.
[16:19] Samuel Pike: What GPU types are you expecting? We run on GCP and Azure — A100s mostly, a few T4s for batch workloads.
[16:20] Dev Patel: For low latency at 99th pct, A100 or H100 class is ideal. We can optimize for A100 with memory-quant and KV cache tuning. If you prefer cost savings we can look at 4-bit quantization options but there's a small quality delta.
[16:22] Tom Reynolds: Quality delta — how big is small? We're sensitive because this is customer-facing.
[16:22] Dev Patel: Typically small for instruction-tuned models, but for domain-specific tokenization you might see regressions. We recommend running an eval set during the pilot to measure quality vs cost.
[16:24] Maria Chen: Timeline — customer asked for pilot within 2-3 weeks. Is that still realistic?
[16:25] Dev Patel: For Dedicated in a private VPC, we need infra provisioning + networking 1 week if network and IP allow lists are ready; then deployment and benchmark 1 week. 2 weeks is tight but doable for a minimal pilot.
[16:26] Priya Nair: Stakeholders include product, SRE, security, and legal for contracts. We want a checklist of gating items.
[16:27] Anika Suresh: I'll own the onboarding runbook and coordinate sprints.
[16:28] Aisha Khan: On legal side we need data processing addendum, data residency confirmation and audit logs for every token-level request.
[16:29] Maria Chen: Redwood Console has token-level traces and audit logs; we can enable long retention as an add-on. We'll share the doc.
[16:30] Samuel Pike: Network — we need the exact CIDR blocks and peering flow. Can you provide recommended firewall rules?
[16:31] Dev Patel: Yes, we'll send an IP allowlist and sample 5-tuple firewall rules. Expect some follow-up on NAT and egress.
[16:33] Tom Reynolds: For the benchmark, we want both throughput and tail latency at 99.9 and 99.99. Can we measure p99.9?
[16:33] Dev Patel: Yes, our benchmark harness emits p50/p95/p99/p99.9 and we can attach traces. Note p99.99 is noisy in short runs; we'll do sustained runs to capture it.
[16:35] Maria Chen: Pricing — we discussed Dedicated blocks earlier but want an official quote. Also are there autoscaling options during burst?
[16:36] Dev Patel: Dedicated supports burst pools; autoscaling policies configurable with warm-up targets. Pricing depends on committed blocks vs on-demand burst. We'll send a pilot pricing sheet with modeled token costs and Dedicated block pricing.
[16:37] Aisha Khan: Any certifications beyond SOC2? We might need ISO 27001 and FedRAMP eventually.
[16:37] Maria Chen: We have SOC2 and ISO materials; FedRAMP is not supported currently. We'll flag that upfront.
[16:38] Lena Ortiz: Rollout plan after pilot — we want a canary to 10% then progressive rollout with automatic fallback to a smaller-capacity model if latency spikes. Is that supported?
[16:39] Dev Patel: Yes, Redwood supports canary and A/B rollouts and automatic fallback policies to compatible model variants. We'll include runbook steps.
[16:41] Tom Reynolds: Integration — how do we handle RBAC and SSO? We need SAML integration and per-team roles.
[16:42] Maria Chen: Redwood supports SSO via SAML/Okta and has RBAC with role templates. We'll send the SSO setup guide.
[16:43] Priya Nair: For data — we need to confirm what is persisted, especially for KV cache and prefix caching. Can we disable caching?
[16:44] Dev Patel: You can disable persistent KV cache; local ephemeral caches exist but persistent prefix caches are opt-in. We'll document the defaults.
[16:45] Aisha Khan: Also, encryption at rest and in-transit must be customer-managed keys.
[16:46] Dev Patel: Supported, with KMS integrations and HSM options for on-prem. Small gotcha: some managed telemetry requires opt-in depending on your compliance posture.
[16:48] Maria Chen: Ok let's recap the immediate next steps — I'll list them and confirm owners. Dev will run a smoke benchmark and send firewall/IP details; Aisha to send compliance contacts; Lena confirm PII/data residency; Maria to share pricing and pilot agreement draft; Anika to own runbook. Any objections?
[16:49] Samuel Pike: Sounds good.
[16:50] Lena Ortiz: One ask — include a short architecture diagram for the VPC peering flow.
[16:50] Dev Patel: We'll include that in the networking package.
[16:51] Tom Reynolds: Also include model-quantization recommendation for our workload, ideally with expected cost delta.
[16:52] Dev Patel: Yep, will include 4-bit vs 8-bit tradeoffs and a recommendation table.
[16:54] Maria Chen: Great, we'll aim to have docs out by Friday. Any final questions?
[16:56] Priya Nair: No, thanks everyone.
[16:57] Maria Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up on the action items and schedule the benchmark. Meeting adjourned.
[16:58] <call ended>
notes: Customer requires private VPC setup; SOC2 and KMS are gating items
Pilot target: Dedicated for predictable tails, 2-week minimum pilot timeline with benchmarking
Redwood to provide networking docs, security artifacts, pricing, and pilot agreement
